Re: Cameron Delgado  
Member ID: W425374190  
Plan: Cigna Commercial/ACA — Idaho  
Reference number: POC-F628C11122-30133  
Requested service: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair  
CPT: 29827  
Treating surgeon: Reyes, MD

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial dated August 1, 2026, which states that the prior-authorization documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. Please conduct a complete medical-necessity review using the enclosed clinical records and reverse the denial.

The submitted records establish the following:

- I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 18 supervised physical-therapy visits over 10 weeks, from May 3 through July 12, 2026. The therapy focused on rotator-cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, and the physical-therapy discharge note documents the course of treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 9, 2026, provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on May 31, 2026, shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- I cannot lift the affected arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side.
- Examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- There is no active infection, untreated substance use, or other stated contraindication. I am a nonsmoker, with a BMI of 29.

These records address the clinical information necessary to evaluate the request: the diagnosis and tear characteristics, imaging findings, duration and severity of symptoms, functional impairment, physical-examination findings, and failure of directed nonsurgical treatment. The MRI documents a full-thickness tear, and the 1.8 cm measurement places it within the small-to-medium full-thickness tear range described in the publicly available Cigna/EviCore shoulder-surgery guideline. The MRI also documents fatty atrophy, which is directly relevant to evaluation of rotator-cuff muscle quality.

The publicly available guideline states: “The determination of medical necessity for the performance of shoulder surgery is always made on a case-by-case basis.” This case should therefore be reviewed using the complete clinical record rather than denied for an unspecified documentation omission. The guideline also states: “Evaluation of rotator cuff muscle quality with CT or MRI is an important consideration.” The May 31 MRI supplies that information.

The records further show persistent, function-limiting symptoms despite an appropriate course of conservative care, including supervised physical therapy, NSAIDs, rest, and injection treatment. The injection produced only temporary partial relief. Continued nonoperative treatment has not restored shoulder function, and the documented full-thickness tear and fatty atrophy support timely surgical evaluation.

Please reconsider and approve CPT 29827. If Cigna maintains the denial, please identify each specific missing document or clinical criterion, provide the exact clinical-review criteria and policy version applied to this request, and provide the clinical rationale for concluding that the records do not establish medical necessity.

Please process this appeal as a pre-service medical-necessity appeal. I request written confirmation of receipt and a written appeal determination.

Sincerely,

Cameron Delgado
